correctness.rationale: All-length common polynomial factors are classified by two nonidentity roots of unity at integer separation h; only separation one and length a multiple of six yield a shared quadratic. Integral monic quotients have a nonzero exact resultant so every normalized GCD divides it and is periodic. At length six an explicit integer Bezout certificate and parity reduce the spectrum to one or seven. At length twelve the 18x18 Sylvester determinant restricts primes to 2,5,7,13; complete root tests and distinct Hensel digits eliminate all p² divisibility. CRT determines eight exact counts and least period 455. The standalone checker verifies the determinant, all root lists, square-lift obstructions, all 455 residue classes and 8000 direct GCD computations. Finite checks do not replace the symbolic all-length proof.

originality.rationale: The 2022 primary source (Komatsu, 11D07) analyzes additive Frobenius representation problems for shifted geometric sequences, explicitly relating them to repunits, but does not characterize equal-length cross-base GCDs. The strongest general GCD papers from 2016, 2020 and 2021 prove resultant boundedness, periodicity or the structure of coprime polynomial-value gcd sets: these general principles are acknowledged and not presented as original. The newly established precise polynomial common-factor classification for every integer shift and length, and the eight-valued length-twelve squarefree local gcd spectrum despite a highly nonsquarefree resultant, were not found or implied by inspected statements. Search cannot certify absolute publication priority.
residual_risks: Older general polynomial-value-GCD studies or unindexed recreational-number-theory literature may contain an equivalent neighboring-base repunit classification or exact length-twelve table.
The proof is same-model reviewed and verified by a standalone exact-arithmetic checker; an independent mathematical or publication-priority audit has not occurred.

value.rationale: The shift-varying equal-length repunit GCD is a natural and previously unclassified simultaneous divisibility invariant complementary to additive repunit representation problems. The theorem gives a rigid all-length/all-shift growth dichotomy, then complete exact 6- and 12-digit normalized spectra and natural densities. The number-theoretic content lies in identifying and sharply resolving exceptional local primes, not simply applying known periodicity machinery.
